subject: Sunfield: Inference topology assurance and threat brief
messages:
From: Sarah Benitez <sarah.benitez@sunfieldhealth.com>

Cc: tom.alvarez@sunfieldhealth.com, procurement@sunfieldhealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Request: network/topology assurance + threat summary for RFP

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As part of Sunfield's security review we need a concise package that covers:

- High-level deployment topology (VPCs, subnets, peering, public egress points)
- Tenant/isolation model (how customer data is partitioned and protected)
- Threat surface summary and mitigation controls (lateral movement, egress, compromised-instance scenarios)
- Sample evidence (network diagram, config/ACL examples, audit log snippet)

Can you provide a short brief and attachments we can include in our RFP response? We aim to close vendor evaluation by Aug 4th.

Appreciate it — if you need a quick alignment call, Tom and I are free early next week.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Benitez
InfoSec Program Manager, Sunfield Health

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Benitez <sarah.benitez@sunfieldhealth.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: network/topology assurance + threat summary for RFP

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. I'm attaching a concise packet that addresses each bullet (see attachment stubs below). High level notes up front:

- Topology: Redwood runs a segmented multi-tenant control plane and per-customer serving VPCs (customer VPCs are logically isolated; we avoid shared-sidecars that access customer tokens). Public egress is restricted to managed egress gateways (bastion NATs) and explicit external endpoints.

- Isolation model: Strong tenant isolation via per-customer tenancy, role-based service accounts, per-tenant keying for model artifact access, and encrypted KV caches. We also offer a Private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) for customers that need network-level tenancy.

- Threat mitigations: Defense-in-depth with network ACLs, host hardening, continuous KV-caching audit, per-request telemetry, and automatic fallback to hardened model variants when anomalous patterns occur.

Next steps: Olga (CC) can add the technical Q&A appendix and a small sample of audit evidence. Marcus can speak to KV/cache isolation and runtime mitigations. Vanessa if you could pick up a 30-min walkthrough slot for next Tue/Wed that'd be great for their procurement/SecOps team.

Attachments (in this thread): sunfield_topology_diagram_v1.pdf; isolation_controls_matrix.xlsx; audit-log-sample.txt

Regards,

Tessa Morgan
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0191

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Benitez <sarah.benitez@sunfieldhealth.com>, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: network/topology assurance + threat summary for RFP

Sarah / Tessa —

Attaching the appendix and a short Q&A below to address likely procurement/security follow-ups. Attachment files are the same as Tessa listed — I have versioned the diagram for annotation.

Key technical clarifications (summary):

1) Per-customer isolation
- Serving: Each customer is assigned a dedicated serving VPC/namespace. Network plane enforces strict security groups and ACLs; there is no flat shared network between tenants.
- Control plane: A hardened control plane handles model lifecycle and billing; control-to-serving communication is authenticated with mutual TLS; control plane does not have access to decrypted customer inputs unless the customer opts into telemetry sharing.

2) Egress controls and allowed destinations
- Outbound access from the serving VPCs is via managed egress gateways (bastion NATs) with allowlists and strict DNS policies.
- Customers can configure additional egress restrictions in Private deployments (e.g., on-prem or VPC endpoints to internal data stores).

3) Compromise scenarios & mitigation
- Compromised worker: processes run in sandboxed runtime with mandatory access controls; instance compromise triggers automated token revocation and KV cache eviction.
- Lateral movement: microsegmentation + host-level firewalling reduce lateral blast radius; flows are audited and anomalous traffic triggers isolations and rollbacks.

4) Keys, secrets, and data at rest
- All customer secrets and model artifacts are encrypted with customer-scoped keys in KMS; we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for Private deployments.

5) Observability & evidence
- Audit logs (immutably stored) include request id, model id, route, source IP, and tokens used for model artifact pulls. We provided a redacted sample: audit-log-sample.txt.

6) Hardening & compliance posture
- SOC 2 controls mapped; periodic pentests and runtime fuzzing; we provide artifact-based evidence on request (config snapshots, signed attestations).

Suggested reading (links are attached): topology diagram (annotated), isolation_controls_matrix.xlsx. If you want specific configs (Security Group ACLs, iptables examples, or egress allowlists) we can share them under an NDA or via a secure link.

Quoted below is the annotated (redacted) snippet from the diagram for quick reference:

"Serving cluster per-tenant -> private subnet -> gpu-hosts (sandboxed runtimes) -> egress via bastion NAT cluster -> monitored egress proxies -> external endpoints (allowlist)"

Happy to expand any item — I can join the walkthrough to cover the threat scenarios and live-demo the audit log search.

--
Olga Petrov
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, this is very helpful. We've downloaded the attachments and reviewed the diagram. A couple quick asks before we include this in the RFP packet:

If you can confirm the above in the next 48 hours, we'll proceed to include Redwood in the shortlist and move to commercial review.

Regards,
Tom Alvarez
